evals.prompt: We're a pure ecommerce brand with no physical presence at all. Should we invest in local marketing?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this skill mostly doesn't apply to an ecom-only business and redirect to seo-audit/ads instead, per the skill's explicit guidance. Should ask if there's any specific local component (a warehouse showroom, a pop-up) before fully ruling it out, but should not force a local marketing plan onto a business with no physical footprint.
assertions: Recognizes local marketing mostly doesn't apply without a physical presence
Redirects to seo-audit/ads as the appropriate alternative
Checks for any specific local component before fully dismissing it
Does not force a full local marketing plan onto a pure ecom business

evals.prompt: We have 50 dealer locations. Can we just require every dealer to post the exact same content on their Google Business Profile?
evals.expected_output: Should push back on a rigid one-size-fits-all approach, recommending a corporate template + local flexibility model instead — consistent baseline (brand voice, NAP format, approved standards) while giving room for genuinely local content. Should note that a rigid template performs worse than one with real local texture, per Multi-Location Coordination guidance.
assertions: Pushes back on a fully rigid, identical-everywhere content requirement
Recommends the corporate template + local flexibility model
Explains why rigid templates underperform ones with local texture

evals.prompt: Our reviews have gotten a bit stale. Should we offer customers a discount for leaving a positive review?
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to recommend incentivizing specifically for positive reviews, flagging this as dishonest, a platform policy violation risking the whole profile, and potentially a compliance issue depending on jurisdiction. Should recommend building a systematic, non-incentivized review-request habit into the natural post-purchase moment instead.
assertions: Refuses to recommend incentivizing positive-only reviews
Flags the platform policy and compliance risk explicitly
Recommends a systematic non-incentivized review-request process instead
Does not simply comply with the discount-for-review request

evals.prompt: We have 200 locations but only budget to really focus on a handful this quarter. How do we pick?
evals.expected_output: Should recommend prioritizing by opportunity rather than treating every location identically — triage by revenue potential, current visibility gap, and competitive local density, per the Multi-Location Coordination guidance. Should flag treating every location the same as a named common mistake to avoid.
assertions: Recommends prioritizing by opportunity (revenue potential, visibility gap, competitive density)
Explicitly avoids recommending equal treatment across all 200 locations
Flags treating every location identically as a mistake to avoid
